stem.en: Kabir says a two-letter code "would have been fine if there were only sixteen amino acids". What else would change?

text.en: Every recipe would be a third shorter, and there would be no spare words at all. With sixteen beads and sixteen words, every possible typo would change the bead. A code with no spare words is the last lesson of this module.

feedback.en: It fits exactly, which means every word is used, and that has a cost you will see in three days.
The number of bead kinds does not set strength. It sets what shapes are possible.

text.en: The code would have to be four letters, not two.

feedback.en: Four cubed is sixty-four; four squared is sixteen. Sixteen words name sixteen beads. Two letters would be enough, and dangerous.

explanation.en: Count words against beads. Sixteen equals sixteen leaves no slack. Slack is what makes the real code forgiving.
